Campaign brief: Resend provides a separately configured route for transactional email through SMTP or official SDKs, with no Resend daily sending limit on paid plans.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Resend provides a separately configured route for transactional email through SMTP or official SDKs, with no Resend daily sending limit on paid plans.
events.arc: Recognize the built-in-sender constraint, announce Resend as a concrete alternative, explain the integration and plan boundary, reduce the perceived cost of a first test, and ask the reader to start evaluating it.

emails.job: Get a problem-aware backend engineer to create a Resend account and assess it as a separate sending route for auth-related transactional email.
emails.single_idea: When a hosted authentication platform’s built-in sender becomes the constraint, Resend gives the team a separate SMTP or SDK-based route for transactional email; paid Resend plans remove the Resend daily sending limit.
emails.objection: Switching sending providers sounds like a migration project I do not have time to take on.
must_not_say: Do not say Resend changes, bypasses, or automatically raises the hosted authentication platform’s own Auth rate limit; that setting must still be adjusted separately.
Do not present the Free plan as an escape from a 100-email-per-day ceiling.
Do not say a complete migration takes 30 minutes; the documented figure covers Raycast’s small waitlist-email test only.
Do not promise unlimited sending; paid plans have no daily limit, but plan quotas and overage terms still apply.
Do not claim Resend detects or survives an upstream Auth Hook clearing SMTP configuration.
Do not claim Resend explains how another platform counts messages against its rate limit.
Do not promise guaranteed deliverability, uninterrupted auth email, or inbox placement.
Do not claim transactional and marketing sending are fully isolated by default.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

Only the paid tiers remove the daily cap; on the free plan the engineer swaps one 100/day ceiling for another, and nothing in the ledger speaks to the auth platform's own rate-limit setting that still has to be raised.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: The hosted platform’s subscription tier does not necessarily change its built-in email limit. The sending route and the platform’s own Auth rate-limit setting must be configured separately.
emails.mechanism: Resend can be connected through SMTP or official SDKs. The Free plan is capped at 100 emails per day, while Pro, Scale, and Enterprise have no Resend daily limit. A narrow first test can precede a broader migration; Raycast completed a test of waitlist emails for its iOS and Windows apps within 30 minutes.
emails.next_step_decision: Whether Resend offers a viable separately configured route for the reader’s auth-related transactional email.
emails.next_step_value: Create an account and begin evaluating Resend through SMTP or an official SDK supported by the reader’s stack.
emails.next_step_limit: Signing up does not validate production deliverability, complete a migration, or update a hosted authentication platform’s separate Auth rate-limit setting.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Resend can be evaluated against failure cases before real recipients or domain reputation are put at risk.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: A basic test endpoint does not necessarily expose the provider’s dashboard, webhook, and API behavior for the delivery events the application must handle.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Resend Test Mode and its designated test recipient addresses simulate delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without sending to real people or affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating a provider requires risking real sends or immediately changing the production flow. After: Resend can first be tested against defined delivery events in a non-production evaluation.
must_not_say: Do not say Test Mode proves production deliverability.
Do not say an API-based simulation validates a hosted authentication platform’s SMTP configuration.
Do not promise that testing detects or prevents an upstream Auth Hook from clearing SMTP settings.
Do not imply simulated events are real inbox-placement tests.
alternative_arguments.objection: I cannot risk testing a new email route against real users or my sending reputation.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Whether Resend’s test environment covers the delivery-event cases the application needs to handle before production integration.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The official page documents this verified fact: Resend supplies test recipient addresses for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: This test does not establish production inbox placement or validate the hosted authentication platform’s SMTP route and rate-limit settings.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Present the launch through a safe, concrete first test rather than a broad claim about reliability.

events.preview_text: Evaluate Resend through SMTP or an official SDK, with clear daily plan limits.
events.body:
Resend is available as a separate route for auth-related transactional email. Connect it through SMTP or an official SDK.

If a hosted authentication platform’s built-in sender becomes the constraint, you can configure Resend as the provider while managing the platform’s own Auth rate-limit setting separately.

The Free plan has a **100 emails per day** limit. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise plans have **no Resend daily limit**; plan quotas and overage terms still apply.

A narrow test can come before a broader migration. Raycast started with waitlist emails for its iOS and Windows apps and completed that test within 30 minutes.

Create an account and begin evaluating Resend through SMTP or an official SDK.

Get started

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Beyond Auth logs: test delivery events"
events.subject: Beyond Auth logs: test delivery events
events.preview_text: Simulate delivery outcomes without sending to real recipients or affecting domain reputation.
events.body:
Checking Auth logs can help verify whether a documented email limit was exceeded. It still leaves separate test paths to be built for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint behavior across a provider’s dashboard, webhooks, and API.

We’re introducing Resend, an email-sending platform for developers to route application-generated messages through an API, official SDKs, or SMTP.

Resend Test Mode provides designated recipient addresses that simulate delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events. No message goes to a real recipient, and the test does not affect your domain reputation.

This does not establish production inbox placement or validate an authentication platform’s SMTP settings. It shows how Resend’s dashboard, webhooks, and API represent the events your application may need to handle.

Review the test email documentation

emails.objection: I need to know the exact Supabase setup and whether I will encounter another quota before I create an account.
must_not_say: Do not state or imply that every recipient has already experienced a 429 error; present it as a relevant conditional scenario.
Do not claim that connecting Resend automatically raises Supabase's Auth rate limit; the engineer must adjust that setting separately.
Do not claim that Resend's Free plan removes daily limits; it is capped at 100 emails per day and 3,000 per month.
Do not promise to explain or correct how Supabase meters sends against its own threshold.
Do not claim Resend detects, prevents, or survives Supabase dashboard actions that clear SMTP configuration.
Do not promise uninterrupted auth email, guaranteed deliverability, or a migration duration.

emails.why_it_fails: Those actions can diagnose or postpone the error, but they do not create the separate SMTP route Supabase requires; upgrading the auth platform alone does not replace its built-in mailer.
emails.mechanism: Resend provides Supabase-specific SMTP instructions and a direct credentials destination. After connecting it, the engineer must still adjust Supabase's initial 30-messages-per-hour Auth limit. emails.call_to_action: Review the Supabase SMTP setup and current Resend plan limits before signing up: https://resend.com/docs/send-with-supabase-smtp and https://resend.com/pricing

emails.next_step_value: The setup guide shows the Supabase-specific SMTP configuration and credentials destination; the pricing page shows the Free and Pro quotas, daily limits, price, and paid overage terms.

events.subject: Send Supabase Auth email with Resend
events.preview_text: Review the SMTP setup and sending limits before signing up.
events.body:
Resend is now available as an external SMTP option for Supabase Auth. You can route account emails through Resend instead of relying on the built-in mailer.

The setup is explicit: open Authentication > Email > SMTP Settings, add your sender details, then paste your Resend SMTP credentials. Supabase initially limits custom-SMTP Auth sending to **30 messages per hour**, which you adjust separately under Auth rate limits.

Resend Free includes **3,000 emails per month**, with a 100-email daily limit. Pro costs $20 per month for 50,000 emails, has no daily limit, and charges $0.90 per 1,000 additional emails.

Review the documented Supabase setup and current plan limits before signing up. Compare both limits with the Auth-email volume you expect.

events.subject: Test Resend events without real sends
events.preview_text: Simulate delivery, bounce, and complaint events without affecting your domain reputation.
events.body:
Resend provides designated test addresses for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events. You can inspect the resulting events through the Dashboard, API, and webhooks without sending messages to real users or affecting your domain reputation.

Resend is an email-sending platform for developers, available as an external SMTP option for Supabase Auth account emails. It provides a bounded way to review event behavior before deciding whether to route production traffic through it.

Send to delivered@resend.dev, bounced@resend.dev, or complained@resend.dev to simulate each outcome. The bounce test returns an SMTP 550 5.1.1 “Unknown User” response, making failure handling visible without using a real recipient.

The official guide documents each test address and its expected event. These simulations show how Resend exposes events; they do not establish production deliverability or confirm the complete Supabase SMTP configuration.
